coefficient_identity.identity: product_{a=1}^n(1+xi_a t) = product_{j=1}^k(1+sum_{i=1}^{p_j} sigma_i(block j)t^i) = 1+sum_{r=1}^n sigma_r(xi_1,...,xi_n)t^r.
coefficient_identity.exact_proof: The coefficient of t^r in the full product is the sum of products of xi_a over all r-element subsets I of {1,...,n}. Intersection with the k consecutive blocks gives a bijection I <-> (I_1,...,I_k), with sum_j |I_j|=r. This bijection preserves the monomial product. Summing first over fixed block cardinalities gives the product of the corresponding elementary symmetric functions. The empty subset contributes1 in each block and in the full product.
coefficient_identity.quotient_map: Apply the coefficientwise ring homomorphism Z[xi_1,...,xi_n] -> A[xi_1,...,xi_n]/(sigma_r-c_r)=C, carrying xi_a to its class. Under this map sigma_r becomes c_r and the block symmetric functions become the defined c_i^(j).

coefficient_identity.meaning_of_weights: The isobaric instruction selects these n coefficient relations. Weight i is a formal bookkeeping weight on the elementary symmetric expressions; no grading on the arbitrary base ring A or on the specialized quotient C is assumed. Merely evaluating the restored polynomial identity at t=1 would not by itself specify all n relations.
